name: Foraminifera
desc: A plankton tow under the objective, drawn Haeckel-style: radiolaria as latticed silica spheres nested one inside another, their geodesic surface pierced by pores and fanning long radial axopodia-spines into a star, alongside foraminifera as calcite trochospirals whose swelling chambers wind out on a log spiral, each domed, pore-stippled and trailing short spines. Every mineral test drifts on a slow bounded orbit, turns on two incommensurate rates and breathes its spines in and out while an oblique light lights the near flank, so the radial forms never read the same twice. Offered as glowing dark-field, an engraved Kunstformen plate, false-colour fluorescence or a cyanotype blueprint.

energy.doc: brightness of the shell glow and lattice edges

scale.doc: magnification - tests swell, guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: drift, rotation, spine breathing and the sweeping light

density.doc: how many tests are in the field

spines.doc: length and prominence of the radial axopodia / chamber spines

hue.doc: base hue of the calcite / silica

style.doc: aesthetic: glowing silica on black / engraved sepia Kunstformen plate / additive false-colour fluorescence / cyanotype blueprint linework

seed.doc: deterministic - re-throws the population, chamber counts and lattice
